memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the Lord must be destroyed." - Exodus 22:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This command was given to Israel as a nation set apart to be wholly devoted to the one true God, surrounded by peoples who worshipped countless idols. Sacrificing to other gods was not a private preference; it was covenant betrayal that would corrupt the entire nation. The severity reflects how completely God claimed His people's worship. We do not enforce Israel's civil law today, yet the truth it guards could not be more relevant.

God alone is worthy of our worship, and He will not share the throne of our hearts with rivals. This is not divine insecurity but reality — He is the only true God, the source of all good, and anything we put in His place will ultimately fail us. Idols today rarely sit on altars; they hide in our love of money, status, comfort, control, or approval. Anything we serve above God has quietly become a "god" we sacrifice to.

Jesus said we cannot serve two masters (Matt 6:24). The call is to wholehearted devotion — not because God is harsh, but because only He can truly satisfy the human heart. Every idol makes promises it cannot keep and demands more than it gives. The living God, by contrast, gave His own Son for us. He is worthy of first place, and He alone can hold it well. What might be quietly competing for the throne of your heart today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What "gods" — money, status, comfort, approval — quietly compete for first place in my heart?
What would wholehearted devotion to God look like for me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You alone are worthy of my worship. Expose the idols that quietly compete for my heart, and draw me back to wholehearted devotion to You, my only true God. Amen.
